newsitem.title: USA: Intel Q3 orders at record, gross margin up.
newsitem.headline: Intel Q3 orders at record, gross margin up.

text.p: Intel Corp said orders received during the third quarter reached a record high and exceeded the sales it booked during the quarter. Consequently its book-to-bill ratio of orders to sales was above 1.O.

Intel also said gross margins jumped to 57.2 percent from 53.5 percent in the second quarter, helped largely by a better product mix. Lower-margin motherboards fell as a percentage of sales relative to microprocessors, which are a higher-margin product.
Intel said revenues grew 11 percent from the second quarter alone, and at $5.14 billion were the first time ever that revenues topped $5 billion in a single quarter.
Earnings per share rose 26 percent from the second quarter.

Andy Grove, Intel chief executive, cited microprocessors for the success. "We are delighted with the excellent acceptance of Pentium and Pentium Pro processor-based PCs and servers, which has produced a stronger third quarter than we had originally expected," Grove said in a statement.
Intel said its net cash rose in the third quarter by $714 million to $6.12 billion.

Expenses in the third quarter rose 31 percent from the year ago third quarter, Intel said, due to strategic investments in products and process technology, higher marketing costs, profit dependent-related expenses, and more employees. Intel added 6,000 employees since the same quarter a year earlier, bringing its staff to 46,000 .
But expenses fell as a percentage of revenues from the second quarter of this year.
